text:
anika: quick check — proposing a 2-stage evaluation protocol for speculative decoding bringup. goal: measure latency/cost gains vs. quality/safety regressions in a controlled, reproducible way. sketch below, please sanity-check.

anika: stage 1 = cheap speculative pass (small model / prune / int8), emit n-best with token-level confidence + kv-cache hints. stage 2 = verify with full model (fp16 or quantized high-accuracy) for final output or fallback.

anika: metrics i'd like to capture: p50/p95 latency, avg tokens consumed (spec + verify), token-cost delta, quality delta (exact-match / BLEU / LLM-eval score), divergence rate (spec output != verify final), hallucination proxy via embed-distance threshold, safety regression counts on curated prompts.

liam: add: track per-step roll-forward rate (how often spec output accepted without verify). gives direct SLO impact for tail latency. also record temperature/topk for each run (they matter a lot).

jordan: for hallucination proxy, +1 for embed-distance, but we should also record answer length and repetition heuristics. sometimes embed distance triggers on stylistic drift not hallucination. maybe a small human eval slice for top offenders.

cheng: think about batching effects — speculative pass will change request size distribution. P95 measured on single-req latency vs batched throughput differ. we should run both single-request and steady-state batch sweeps. note GPU kernel selection change between int8 vs int4 can flip latency ordering.

maya: happy to run the first sweep tomorrow. what's the canonical model/quant pairs? i'm thinking: llama3-13b fp16 (verify) + llama2-7b int8 (spec), and also a quant-probe: llama3-13b int4 spec + fp16 verify to see same-model hybrid.

anika: exactly. include cross-model combos + same-model quant hybrids. seeds: run 3 random seeds per config, and fix prompt set. offline holdout: 10k prompts stratified by length (short/med/long) and domain (code/chat/qa/rg).

liam: for deterministic comparison, also run "deterministic decode" (topk/tem=0) baseline — helps isolate sampling noise from spec artifacts.

jordan: logging format: JSONL per request with fields: req_id, seed, config, spec_tokens, verify_tokens, accepted(boolean), spec_text, verify_text, embed_dist, safety_flags. small example: 
```
{"req_id":"r123","config":"7b-int8->13b-fp16","spec_tokens":42,"verify_tokens":10,"accepted":true} 
```
(we'll expand fields later)

cheng: make sure to log GPU/host mem and kernel name (for perf triage). kernel name helps explain weird latency spikes when switching quant kernels.

maya: job submission command i'll use: 
```bash
redwood-run --image=ml-eval:prod --prompts=gs://redwood-eval/spec2k/holdout-10k.jsonl --configs=configs/spec-sweep.yaml --out=gs://redwood-eval/results/spec-sweep-$(date +%s).jsonl
```
will tag runs with git sha and experiment id.

devops-bot: Job created: run-2026-03-21-09-12, q: high, cluster: ml-sweep-2. Logs -> https://internal.redwood/jobs/run-2026-03-21-09-12

anika: nice. one more: acceptance criterion for rollout = average quality delta <= 0.5% on primary metric OR human judged no critical regressions, and roll-forward rate >= 85% for latency tier. open to tweak thresholds.

liam: +please include cost-per-1000-requests projection (we have a cost model) — helps PMs weigh tradeoffs.

jordan: i'll prep a small human-eval rubric for halluc/safety triage and a notebook to sample top-100 divergence cases automatically.

maya: starting sweeps in ~1h. i'll post run ids and a short dashboard (p95 latency, accept rate, avg token delta) when first batch finishes. :rocket:

cheng: ping me if you want kernel telemetry aggregated (I can add an exporter).

anika: thanks all. if no objections i'll merge this into the onboarding playbook and we can iterate after first results. :thumbsup:

liam: sounds good.

jordan: lgtm.

maya: on it.
